checks.do: Before comparing shadow IT counts, confirm the time period and filters; the default period is the last 7 days.
For an API question, check the zins package and the GraphQL endpoint before saying there is no SDK; the Python SDK has one.

ssr-what.statement: The report's own page, which calls it Shadow IT, breaks applications down by status, sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified or under review, and by their number of users.

quotes: The Shadow IT gives a breakdown of applications by their status — sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified, or under review and their number of users.

ssr-scale.statement: Zscaler says the report supports up to 50K cloud applications.

quotes: Zscaler supports up to 50K cloud applications.

ssr-risk-index.statement: Each application carries a risk index from 1 (lowest risk) to 5 (highest risk).

quotes: (1–5, 1 being the lowest risk and 5 being the highest)

ssr-features.statement: Its listed benefits include discovering and managing shadow IT applications used by the organization's users, departments or locations, and scrutinizing applications across multiple risk attributes.

quotes: Discover and manage shadow IT applications used by your organization's user, department, or location.
Gain comprehensive visibility and assurance for SaaS applications by scrutinizing them across multiple risk attributes

ssr-default-period.statement: The report can show the last 1 day, 7 days, 15 days, month or quarter, and its default period is the last 7 days.

quotes: You can view data from the last 1 day, 7 days, 15 days, month, or quarter. The default time period is the last 7 days.

ssr-path.statement: The report's page is at Data Security > Inline CASB > Shadow IT.

quotes: On the Shadow IT page (Data Security > Inline CASB > Shadow IT)

ssr-export.statement: The report can be scheduled daily, weekly or monthly, and downloaded as a CSV file; scheduled reports are managed on the Scheduled Reports page under Analytics > Reports > Interactive Reports.

quotes: Schedule a daily, weekly, or monthly Shadow IT Report.
You can view and manage your scheduled Shadow IT Report on the Scheduled Reports page (Analytics > Reports > Interactive Reports > Scheduled Reports).
Download the report as a CSV file.

ssr-endpoint.statement: The Analytics API's production GraphQL endpoint is `https://api.zsapi.net/zins/graphql`, and the API can be accessed via the OneAPI gateway.

quotes: can be accessed via the OneAPI gateway
Production: https://api.zsapi.net/zins/graphql

appinfo-shadow-it-page.statement: The Application Information page shows information on the specific application selected on the Shadow IT page.

quotes: The Application Information page shows you information on the specific application you selected to view on the Shadow IT page.

appinfo-risk-override.statement: On the Application Information page the Zscaler-computed risk index (1-5, 1 the lowest risk and 5 the highest) can be altered and overridden with the Edit icon; the Zscaler-computed index is unavailable for custom cloud applications, whose risk index can nevertheless be edited or reset.

quotes: You can alter and override the Zscaler-computed risk index for the application by clicking the Edit icon (1–5, 1 being the lowest risk and 5 being the highest).
The Zscaler-computed risk index is unavailable for custom cloud applications. However, you can edit or reset their risk index as needed.

appinfo-status-values.statement: The Application Information page's Application Status is sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified or under review.

quotes: Application Status: The application status, whether it's sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified, or under review.

appinfo-bytes-caveat.statement: The total bytes shown might not equal the sum of upload and download bytes, because the uploaded and downloaded bytes distribution data might not be available for the Web Search application.

quotes: the total bytes might not be equivalent to the sum of upload and download bytes because the uploaded and downloaded bytes distribution data might not be available for the Web Search application.

appinfo-1000-rows.statement: The Users table shows data for up to 1,000 entries and Download CSV file gives the data for all entries; the Location table shows unauthenticated location-specific data for the application and is visible only for reports generated by the Zscaler service.

quotes: The table shows data for up to 1,000 entries. You can click Download CSV file to view the data for all the entries.
View the unauthenticated location-specific data for the application in this table.
The Location Table is only visible for reports generated by the Zscaler service.

appinfo-policies-applied.statement: Policies Applied lists all the policies configured specifically for the application in the Zscaler Admin Console and stays blank if none are configured for it.

quotes: Policies Applied: All the policies that are configured specifically for the application in the Zscaler Admin Console. The field stays blank if you haven't configured any policies for the application.

appinfo-3p-integrations.statement: For data to be populated the application must have at least one integration (Risk Attributes > Basic Information); the Risk Attributes and 3rd-Party Integrations information is unavailable for custom cloud applications; and seeing more needs an Internet & SaaS (ZIA) super admin in an organization that has Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance.

quotes: The application must have at least one integration (Risk Attributes > Basic Information) for data to be populated.
The Risk Attributes and 3rd-Party Integrations information is unavailable for custom cloud applications.
you must be a Internet & SaaS (ZIA) super admin and your organization must have Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance.

quotes: The Internet of Things (IoT) Report shows the device inventory and its insights discovered from unauthenticated web traffic.

ssr-rename.title: Whether the product was renamed from the Shadow IT Report
ssr-rename.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Renamed. Originally "Shadow IT Report" (ZINS naming), now marketed as "SaaS Security Report" in current help docs.' The report's own page now names it the Shadow IT Report, so the legacy direction (Shadow IT first, SaaS Security later) is not supported by page text; the old URL survives only as an alias in capture metadata. The Python SDK calls the domain Z-Insights SHADOW_IT, which supports the ZINS alias but not the rename history.

ssr-iot.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report gives IoT device visibility
ssr-iot.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Reporting product covering Shadow IT discovery (unsanctioned cloud apps users access), IoT device visibility, and SaaS-app risk reporting.' The SaaS Security Report capture does not mention IoT devices; IoT device visibility is described by a separate capture (about-iot-report.json).
ssr-iot.resolution: Resolved: IoT device inventory is in the IoT Report (claim ssr-iot-report), not the SaaS Security Report.

ssr-zia.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report is powered by ZIA traffic
ssr-zia.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Powered by traffic flowing through ZIA; extracts visibility signals from existing ZIA telemetry.' The capture places the report under Data Security > Inline CASB > Shadow IT and mentions allowed and blocked transactions, but does not state its data source.

ssr-enforcement.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report enforces policy
ssr-enforcement.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Not a policy-enforcement product; pure observability.' The capture describes discovery, risk review and reporting, and says nothing about enforcement either way.

ssr-8500.title: Older catalogue size in marketing material
ssr-8500.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Some marketing material still cites the older 8,500+ figure — outdated.' No captured page gives an 8,500-application figure.
ssr-8500.resolution: Resolved: no captured page gives an 8,500 figure; the current help states up to 50K cloud applications (claim ssr-scale).

ssr-no-sdk.title: Whether the Go SDK has a Z-Insights module
ssr-no-sdk.detail: The vendored Go SDK tree has no zins package, so Go callers would use direct GraphQL with OneAPI auth; upstream Go releases newer than the vendored tree are unchecked. The Python SDK does have one (ssr-sdk).

report-name.summary: The report's own page and the audit-log page call it the Shadow IT Report, while the NSS page still says SaaS Security Report; whether they mean the same report is not stated. The Gen AI, Posture Management, 3rd-Party App Governance and Activities pages also use SaaS Security Report, as a container for other pages.

report-name.impact: Searching documentation or audit logs by one name may miss material recorded under the other, and the pages use SaaS Security Report both for the Shadow IT report and as a container for posture, app governance, assets and activity pages, so an answer has to say which page it means.
